quizName: DMV Practice Test #4 25 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: When passing parked cars on a motorcycle, you should be ready for:

options.text: Empty parking spaces.
A car to suddenly pull out of a parking space into traffic.
Parking meters.
Other drivers to see you and move out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: A car to suddenly pull out of a parking space into traffic.
questions.explanation: When passing parked cars, be ready for one to suddenly pull out into traffic. Ride on the left side of your lane when passing parked cars on your right. This gives you more space between your motorcycle and any dangers.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger on a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Have a seat large enough for two people.
Have only one set of footrests.
Tell your passenger not to wear protective clothing.
Put a sticker on the brake light to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a seat large enough for two people.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle must have a seat designed for two riders. It should have footrests for your passenger. Your passenger should wear the same protective gear that you wear.

questions.question: Even when it is obvious you will turn, you should:

options.text: Not use a turn signal.
Use a turn signal.
Only use a turn signal if pedestrians are nearby.
Only use a turn signal at a stop light.

questions.explanation: Always use a turn signal every time you turn or change lanes. Use it even if you think others can see what you are doing. Other vehicles may be nearby that you cannot see.

questions.question: Since most crashes happen during daylight, you should:

options.text: Not ride during the day.
Always wear bright clothing.
Ride on the shoulder away from traffic.
Always wear dark clothing.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Always wear bright clothing when riding. This helps other drivers see you, even in daylight.

questions.question: During the day, you should:

options.text: Not turn on your headlight.
Turn on your headlight only if it is cloudy.
Always ride with your headlight on.
Use your headlight if you think it helps.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always ride with your headlight on.
questions.explanation: Always keep your headlight on when riding, even during the day. This makes other drivers twice as likely to notice you.

questions.question: You should inspect your motorcycle:

options.text: Before every ride.
About once every 10 rides.
Once a month.
Once a season.

questions.explanation: A small problem on a motorcycle is much more serious than on a car. Inspect your motorcycle before every ride to stay safe.

questions.question: An approved helmet:

options.text: Lets you see to the sides as much as you need.
Limits how far you can see to the sides.
Is usually uncomfortable.
Has no markings or labels.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets you see to the sides as much as you need.
questions.explanation: An approved helmet allows you to see to the sides safely. It has labels with the maker's name, instructions, and the standards it meets.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a slippery surface?

options.text: A gravel road
Leaves on the road
An icy patch
Dry concrete

questions.explanation: Many surfaces give poor grip for tires. These include wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lines, and metal covers. Dry pavement is safer for motorcycles than these surfaces.

questions.question: To lower your chance of a crash, you should:

options.text: Ride within a foot of the car in front of you.
Wear dark clothing.
Use turn signals only when you want to.
Stay alert and be ready to avoid a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay alert and be ready to avoid a crash.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, stay visible to others. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show what you plan to do. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and to the sides.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol and wait one hour per drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
You may still have side effects from the alcohol.
You will be safe as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may still have side effects from the alcohol.
questions.explanation: Your body removes about one drink's worth of alcohol per hour. However, alcohol can build up in your system. Your ability to ride safely and your judgment can still be hurt.

questions.question: After a motorcycle helmet is in a crash, what should you do?

options.text: Look it over carefully.
Get a new one.
Give it to another rider.
Put a new chinstrap on it.

questions.explanation: Replace your helmet if it has been in a crash.

questions.question: When should you keep more space between your motorcycle and the car ahead?

options.text: When it will be harder to stop than normal.
When you want to see the scenery.
To make other drivers cut you off.
To hide from the driver in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it will be harder to stop than normal.
questions.explanation: Keep extra space when stopping will take longer. This applies when roads are wet, you cannot see ahead, or traffic is heavy.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What is important to remember about motorcycle blind spots in traffic?

options.text: Motorcycles are too small to have blind spots.
Blind spots are so small they do not cause problems.
You need to turn your head to check them.
Motorcycles have only one blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: You need to turn your head to check them.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Always turn your head to check your blind spots before changing lanes.

questions.question: What kind of soles should motorcycle riding shoes have?

options.text: Hard, strong, and slip-resistant.
Thin to let feet breathe.
With tall heels.
Soft and thin.

questions.explanation: Wear boots or shoes that are sturdy and high enough to support your ankles. The soles should be hard, strong, and slip-resistant.

questions.question: If you ride on the right side of your lane behind a car, what happens?

options.text: The driver will see you best.
The driver may not see you unless they use the side mirror.
The driver will know you are there.
Other drivers will not share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver may not see you unless they use the side mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane so the driver ahead can see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check rearview mirrors more often than side mirrors.

questions.question: What does long-term wind noise exposure do?

options.text: It is good for you.
It can damage your hearing.
It is not harmful.
It is safer than listening to music.

questions.explanation: Wind noise while riding can harm your hearing, even with a helmet. Use hearing protection to prevent damage.

questions.question: If you wait one hour after each drink before riding, what happens?

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Alcohol will not affect your skills.
Alcohol effects may still be present.
You are fine as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol effects may still be present.
questions.explanation: Your body removes about one drink of alcohol per hour. However, alcohol can still build up in your system and affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: What should motorcycle passengers do?

options.text: Lean with the operator.
Hold onto the seat.
Sit as far back as possible.
Never hold the operator.

questions.explanation: Passengers should sit directly behind the operator and lean as the operator leans. Hold onto the operator's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: Which is NOT important when choosing a motorcycle helmet?

options.text: It meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards.
It fits snug all the way around your head.
It has no cracks or loose padding.
It looks cool.

questions.explanation: Check that your helmet meets U.S. DOT standards, fits snug all the way around your head, and has no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: Riding at night is usually:

options.text: Easier than riding during the day because you can see the lights of other vehicles better.
Harder than riding during the day because it is more difficult to see.
Not allowed on highways.
Less distracting than riding during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Harder than riding during the day because it is more difficult to see.
questions.explanation: Riding safely at night is harder because you cannot see as well and other drivers cannot see you as well. Without normal daylight, it is harder to judge how far away things are.

questions.question: If wearing footwear with laces, the laces:

options.text: Should be tucked in.
Should hang loose.
Should be removed from the footwear.
Should be glued together.

questions.explanation: Tuck in your shoe laces when riding so they do not get caught on your motorcycle.

questions.question: Taking corners too fast:

options.text: Can cause the rider to move into another lane.
Is better than going too slowly.
Often keeps the rider in their lane.
Is acceptable because motorcycles are smaller than other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause the rider to move into another lane.
questions.explanation: Taking a corner too fast can cause you to move into another lane or go off the road. Slow down before you begin a turn or curve.

questions.question: To protect a motorcycle rider, pants should:

options.text: Be made of soft material.
Be made of heavy material.
Fit loosely so they flap in the wind.
Be short and expose parts of the legs.

questions.explanation: Wear pants made of leather or another strong material that cover your entire legs. Your clothing should fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind, but not so tight that it limits your movement.

questions.question: When selecting footwear, you should choose:

options.text: Shoes with long heels.
Shoes with long laces that cannot be tucked in.
Shoes that cover your ankles.
Shoes made from flimsy materials.

questions.explanation: Wear boots or shoes that are tall and sturdy enough to cover and support your ankles. Heels should be short so they do not catch on surfaces. Tuck in laces so they cannot catch on the motorcycle.
